texts.preamble: M.A. Mubeen, vs The State Of Ap Rep By Its Pp Hyd., Trgh ... on 26 September, 2022 Author: Juvvadi Sridevi Bench: Juvvadi Sridevi The Hon'Ble Smt. Justice Juvvadi Sridevi Criminal Revision Case No.956 Of 2008 Order:
texts.facts: The case of the prosecution, in brief, is as follows: The petitioner/accused No.1 is running a Tea Depot at Narayanapet. On 28.12.2001, PW1/Complainant-Food Inspector inspected the said Tea Depot along with PW3- K.Vijaya Kumar and purchased 450 grams of tea powder for Rs.26-10 ps., and obtained cash receipt from accused No.1, sealed the said tea powder under cover of panchanama by following due procedure and on further enquiry, the complainant came to know that the said tea powder was supplied by A2 and A3. After seizure of the samples, he sent the same for analysis and public analyst after examination, found that it contained iron filings and as such it is adulterated. Subsequently, the complainant obtained written consent for initiating prosecution against the accused person and thereafter, complaint was filed by PW1-Food Inspector against the petitioner herein along with A2 and A3. 3. The accused were examined under Section 251 Cr.P.C., and substance of accusation was stated to them. Accused pleaded not guilty of the offence alleged and claimed to be tried. During the course of trial, prosecution examined P.Ws.1 to 3 and got marked Exs.P.1 to P.32. On behalf of the petitioners/accused, no evidence, either oral or documentary, has been adduced. Aggrieved thereby, the petitioner herein preferred Criminal Appeal No.25 of 2007 on the file of I Additional Sessions Judge, Mahabubnagar. Hence the present Criminal Revision Case.
texts.arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that this Criminal Revision Case is filed challenging the conviction of the petitioner/accused No.1, under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of PFA Act, 1954 on the allegations for selling the Tea Powder containing iron filings on 12.09.2006 to the Food Inspector. 7. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent - State submitted that as per the orders dated 02.11.2017 issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the Commissioners of Food Safety of all the States were directed not to launch for non-conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016 and were advised to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that this Criminal Revision Case is filed challenging the conviction of the petitioner/accused No.1, under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of PFA Act, 1954 on the allegations for selling the Tea Powder containing iron filings on 12.09.2006 to the Food Inspector. 7. The learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the respondent - State submitted that as per the orders dated 02.11.2017 issued by the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India, the Commissioners of Food Safety of all the States were directed not to launch for non-conformance of limit of iron filings for cases where samples were picked up/tested prior to 19.05.2016 and were advised to withdraw all such prosecutions launched prior to 19.05.2016 either under FSS Act, 2006 or PFA Act, 1954.
